subject.title: [Feature Request] Add config encryption for credentials at rest

question: Which credential-at-rest model should OpenClaw support for stored gateway, channel, and provider secrets?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent design changes key custody, recovery, unattended startup, migration behavior, and auth/provider compatibility, so automation should not choose it without maintainer/security intent.

options.title: Design native credential-at-rest storage
options.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, residue cleanup, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and coverage for config plus auth-profile SQLite rows.

options.title: Keep SecretRefs as the supported mitigation
options.body: Explicitly decide that transparent encryption is out of scope for now and narrow remaining work to docs, audit checks, and migration guidance.

options.title: Stage partial hardening first
options.body: Land a smaller opt-in sealing or resolver path while keeping this issue open for openclaw.json, backups, key management, and migration completion.

recommendation.title: Design native credential-at-rest storage
recommendation.body: Define a keychain or passphrase-backed storage model with doctor migration, residue cleanup, recovery behavior, rotation guidance, and coverage for config plus auth-profile SQLite rows.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main history signal across the inspected docs, SecretRef, and auth persistence surfaces, and the unresolved choice is product/security architecture rather than a narrow patch.
